te: Handing public transport powers to local governments, and bus services in 6 provinces
se: The meeting considered decentralising public transport to local government organisations and their results in 6 provinces. So far the Department of Land Transport has handed over only the running of bus terminals; the power to run bus services is still unclear, which limits licensing, hiring private operators and managing fare income. The meeting compared the parts of the draft Land Transport Act on decentralisation, and agreed to gather issues and suggestions so it can offer observations when the draft law comes before the Senate. Local governments in Phuket, Chiang Mai, Lamphun, Songkhla, Samut Sakhon and Kanchanaburi provinces use different investment and management models, and face limits in costs, losses, passenger numbers, the fit of routes and bus sizes, and rules on hiring private operators. The meeting took note and will use this information to study a suitable service model for the main cities of the Northeast, starting with Ubon Ratchathani province as the first study area.
it: Decentralising public transport to local governments, and the draft Land Transport Act
Local government bus services in 6 provinces and the limits they face
Use this information to study a service model, starting with Ubon Ratchathani province

te: Meeting summary video · Handing public transport powers to local governments, and bus services in 6 provinces
Ubon Ratchathani: 3 pilot routes that do not overlap existing routes
se: The meeting considered the status of existing routes and operating rights, and how to arrange a public transport network in Ubon Ratchathani province, hearing OTP and the Department of Land Transport. OTP proposed a network of 17 bus routes covering about 78 per cent of the population, or 180,000 people, with 105 buses in the first phase. There are 47 existing routes (14 in category 1 and 33 in category 4), 13 of which have no operator. Most of the proposed network overlaps existing routes, but 3 routes do not: routes 7, 14 and 17. Problems include existing operators making losses and not ready to invest in new buses, some existing routes being roundabout and slow, and a lack of bus stops, footpaths, depots and charging stations. The meeting suggested small electric buses of about 20 seats, loop routes, checking the travel model against real passenger data and GPS, support for operators to change buses such as low-interest loans, and local governments as the main responsible bodies. The meeting agreed in principle to consider the feasibility of the 3 pilot routes, and asked for information on local government bus services in 6 provinces (Phuket, Samut Sakhon, Songkhla, Lamphun, Chiang Mai and Kanchanaburi) at the next meeting.
it: OTP's proposed network of 17 bus routes, and the Department of Land Transport's data on 47 existing routes
5 observations, such as small electric buses, loop routes and support for operators to change buses
Consider the feasibility of 3 pilot routes: routes 7, 14 and 17
Information on local government bus services in 6 provinces, for the next meeting

te: Meeting summary video · Ubon Ratchathani: 3 pilot routes that do not overlap existing routes
Starting the study: public buses in Khon Kaen, Udon Thani, Ubon Ratchathani and Nakhon Ratchasima
se: The meeting noted its appointment order and set how it will work: it will study the problems, readiness and limits of public transport in Khon Kaen, Udon Thani, Ubon Ratchathani and Nakhon Ratchasima provinces. The Office of Transport and Traffic Policy and Planning (OTP) described its master plan for public transport in 11 main regional cities, which covers all 4 provinces. In 2024 public transport made up on average 3.27 per cent of trips, with targets of 5 per cent in 2027, 10 per cent in 2032 and 20 per cent in 2037. The proposed model is low-floor electric buses running to a timetable every 10–30 minutes, a flat fare of 15 baht and a common ticket system. The state would invest in infrastructure such as bus stops, depots and charging stations, while private operators would provide the buses and run the service. The meeting raised points about the rights of existing route operators, the readiness of local governments, and state support for routes with few passengers, and heard about a bus service in Ubon Ratchathani province that carries about 10 passengers per trip on average. The meeting asked the Department of Land Transport and OTP to compile the status of existing routes and operating rights in the 4 provinces, to compare with the network OTP proposes, and to bring the Ubon Ratchathani information to the next meeting.
it: OTP's master plan for public transport in main regional cities, and the proposed electric bus model
Observations on existing operating rights, local government readiness and state support
Department of Land Transport and OTP to compile the status of existing routes in the 4 provinces, and bring Ubon Ratchathani information to the next meeting
